query: For high-entropy-alloy bond coats used in thermal barrier coating systems for high-temperature applications, what single intervention could improve coating durability and reliability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should remain effective, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The use of an intermediate layer of CoFe2Ni between the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) and the AISI 304 stainless steel substrate can improve the coating durability and reliability of thermal barrier coating systems for high-temperature applications.
generation.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy and AISI 304 stainless steel substrate
generation.intervention: Application of an intermediate layer of CoFe2Ni
generation.conditions: High-temperature applications, laser metal deposition process
generation.mechanism: Accommodation of residual stresses and variation in chemistry change between the AlCoCrFeNi HEA and the AISI 304 substrate
generation.baseline: Direct coating of AlCoCrFeNi HEA on AISI 304 substrate without intermediate layer
generation.uncertainty: Limited studies on the viability of intermediate layers between AlCoCrFeNi HEA and AISI 304 substrate

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of coating durability and reliability with and without intermediate layer of CoFe2Ni
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coating durability and reliability with the intermediate layer of CoFe2Ni are not significantly improved compared to the direct coating without intermediate layer, the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
Through laser metal deposition, attempts were made to coat AlCoCrFeNi, a high-entropy alloy (HEA), on an AISI 304 stainless steel substrate to integrate their properties. However, the direct coating of the AlCoCrFeNi HEA on the AISI 304 substrate was found to be unviable due to cracks at the interface between these two materials. The difference in compositional change was suspected to be the source of the cracks. Therefore, a new transition route was performed by coating an intermediate layer of CoFe2Ni on the AISI 304 substrate. Investigations into the microstructure, phase composition, elemental composition and Vickers hardness were carried out in this study. Consistent metallurgical bonding was observed along both of the interfaces. It was found that the AlCoCrFeNi alloy solidified into a dendritic microstructure. The X-ray diffraction pattern revealed a transition of the crystal structure of the AISI 304 substrate to the AlCoCrFeNi HEA. An intermediate step in hardness was observed between the AISI 304 substrate and the AlCoCrFeNi HEA. Further, AlCoCrFeNi HEA solidified with dendritic and interdendritic microstructures due to elemental segregation. Dendritic segregation regions were found to be Al- and Ni-rich, while interdendritic areas were Fe- and Cr-rich, and the distribution of Co was uniform. Body-centered cubic (BCC) Fe and Cr precipitates, and B2 (ordered BCC) Al- and Ni-rich matrices were observed in previous studies [,,,,]. Most of these studies are based on material fabricated through processes such as casting and arc melting. Unlike these early studies, laser metal deposition (LMD) was implemented in this study.
LMD is capable of fabricating freeform three-dimensional metallic components [,,] and has been used to fabricate several HEAs [,,,,]. Chen et al. fabricated AlxCoFeNiCu1-x (x = 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 atom %, respectively) HEAs using elemental powders on the AISI 304 substrate. They reported an increase in hardness with an increase in aluminum content []. ermal expansion (CTE, 10−6/K) for AlCoCrFeNi HEA was 9.03 (293–303 K), 12.47 (368–378 K) and 13.54 (423–773 K) []. However, the CTE values of AISI 304 were 14.7 (293 K), 16.3 (400 K), 19.5 (700 K) and 20.2 (800 K) []. Harihar et al. observed crack formation at the bottom of an AlCoCrFeNi deposit when deposited on an AISI 304 substrate. Due to the brittleness of the deposited material, the deposit broke off from the AISI 304 substrate easily []. An extensive network of cracks occurred when a TiVCrAlSi HEA was cladded on a Ti-6Al-4V substrate. This was attributed to the difference between the thermal expansion coefficients and residual stresses associated with the high cooling rate in laser cladding [].
